title: Lights and short winter outings in the Gulf of Saint-Tropez
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: At the end of the year, the most fitting outing is not always the longest one. A lit harbour, a lively square or a small market can be enough for a real evening.
content:
Winter in the gulf is not suited to grand promises. It works much better with short late-afternoon or early-evening outings: a lit old centre, a few stalls, a harbour passage, a warm drink and a short but well-chosen walk.

Accept the short format

A small outing is not an incomplete version of the gulf. In December and January it is often the fairest one: one or two hours, a centre, a few lights, some movement and an easy return.

Choose a place that shows clearly

For that brevity to stay pleasant, the place must be easy to review: a harbour, a square, an old village or a market installed in a tight perimeter. That is what avoids unnecessary driving or dispersing the evening.

Keep an eye on weather and the programme

In winter, wind, rain or a reduced programme can quickly change the quality of an outing. The right reflex is to confirm that the event is really happening and to accept giving up when the evening frame becomes less clear than expected.
